fatal_errors: The proposed elevated-temperature constant-load experiment does not reconstruct the room-temperature nanoindentation-creep regime.
It omits modulation-period variation and the decisive comparison among coherent, semicoherent, and grain-boundary-dominated multilayers.

It proposes suppression of atomic diffusion by semicoherent interfaces, whereas the target mechanism invokes pileup-induced interfacial amorphization that enables rate-limited diffusion or interface slip.
The single-phase baseline cannot isolate interface coherency from phase constitution and other microstructural differences.
explanation: The hypothesis addresses creep of an FCC/BCC HEA coating and provides a measurable comparison and clear falsification rule, so it is experimentally testable. It also captures one component of the target mechanism: semicoherent interfaces can obstruct dislocations and produce pileups. However, it misses the governing modulation-period/interface-coherency transition, the approximately 16 nm optimum, the coherent and grain-boundary baselines, the room-temperature 5 mN nanoindentation conditions, and the stress-exponent signature of a transition from dislocation creep to diffusion/interface-slip creep. Its elevated-temperature single-phase comparison is a different study and introduces confounding changes in phase constitution. E1 concerns phase-boundary-mediated deformation rather than sustained creep and includes dislocation transfer across boundaries; E2 concerns gamma/gamma-prime interfaces in a different alloy architecture. Thus, the citations support only a generic interface-strengthening rationale, not the proposed FCC/BCC semicoherent-interface mechanism under the stated conditions.
